answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because bridge only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
